This place was the Library of Eternity, a library so vast and so deep and so well-kept that no librarian had ever turned away a reader who had yet to be born. Its shelves, lined with books of every conceivable color and bound in materials that had no equal in the arts of binding, stretched away from the observer until the edges of the library seemed to meet the sky itself.

The Library was a repository of all thought that had ever existed, of all thought that was yet to exist, and of all thought that had transpired in an age long since passed. It was a place of silence, a place of whispers, a place of endless reading and writing, of erasure and rediscovery, of wisdom and madness. In it, time did not mark the passage of its pages, for the Library was the soul of time, containing within its walls the essence of existence in its many dimensions.

To enter the Library was to cross a threshold that marked the boundary between us and the comprehension of all things.
